narrative.overview: A control room you hold in one hand at 1 a.m. The canvas is near-black under a faint coral-and-blue nebula wash. Everything sits on soft glass panels lit from a hairline above. The only spectacle is the live nebula orb. It is the logo, the Talk button and a status light, and it glows more while agents work. Everything else is quiet, so the two agent colours read instantly: coral means Claude, blue means Codex.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas, glass panels, hairline borders.
Agent identity carried by colour (coral Claude, blue Codex, violet Hermes / Codex cloud, mint OpenCode).
One live signature, the canvas nebula orb. Everything else is still.
Big tabular numerals for usage, Geist everywhere, mono only for data.

rules.name: The Agent Owns Its Colour Rule
rules.body: Coral and blue mean Claude and Codex, nothing else. A third use of coral for "accent" would make the status dots lie.

rules.name: The Signal Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only as state: health dots, error panels, a meter at ≥80%.

rules.name: The Numerals Are Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that is compared or ticks (usage, ms, counts) uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The One Glass Layer Rule
rules.body: Panels don't nest. A list inside a panel uses hairline-divided rows, never cards inside a card.

dos: Do colour anything agent-related with that agent's own colour (claude-coral, codex-blue, hermes-violet).
Do keep rows at least 56px tall and every action within thumb reach on a 390px screen.
Do show an honest empty state when data is missing. Never a demo number.
Do use real icons (lucide, 1.75 stroke) for every arrow and affordance.
donts: Don't add business or finance demo cards. Lind ruled them out.
Don't nest panels or use coloured side-stripes on rows.
Don't use text glyphs (→, ↗) as icons.
